general_information.Description: Multimodal AI course aim on building AI systems that operate across modalities - vision, language, audio, video, 3D, and embodiment. The course frames multimodality through four core problems (representation, alignment, fusion, translation) and proceeds through cross-modal representations (CLIP, SigLIP, ImageBind), fusion architectures (cross-attention, Perceiver, Q-Former, gated cross-attention), vision-language and unified models (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, Chameleon/Janus families), speech and audio, video and world models, 3D and embodied agents, multimodal reasoning / agents / RAG, evaluation (benchmark saturation, hallucination), efficiency and deployment, and safety/provenance/frontiers. Mathematical depth is assumed from the prerequisites (Deep Learning, Advanced Generative AI); this course focuses on architectures, training recipes, evaluation, and hands-on multimodal systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: `- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all labs and the capstone project, and submitting on time. - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes. - Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information. - Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each assignment, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work.
general_information.Tools: `- Python 3.10+ with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers - Google Colab or Jupyter Notebook (GPU access for labs) - A code/text editor (e.g., VS Code) - Open-weight VLMs (LLaVA/SigLIP/Whisper families) - Datasets via Hugging Face Datasets (COCO, VQA, AudioSet, video benchmarks)
general_information.Note: `1) On-going Assessment - Progress Test: 15% - Report 1 - Project proposal: 5% - Report 2 - Representation & Fusion milestone : 10% - Report 3 - Integrated prototype milestone: 10% - Report 4 - Evaluation & Analysis milestone: 10% - Final Presentation: 20% 2) 1 Final Exam: 30% 3) Final Result: 100% Completion Criteria: 1) Every on-going assessment component > 0 2) Capstone Project > 0 3) Final Exam Score >= 4 & Final Result >= 5

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify and characterize multimodal AI systems and the four core problems of multimodal machine learning - representation, alignment, fusion, and translation.
Build cross-modal representations using contrastive and self-supervised methods, and evaluate them via zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval.
Design and implement fusion architectures (cross-attention, latent bottlenecks, connector modules) that combine heterogeneous modalities.
Apply vision-language and unified multimodal architectures (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, and unified token/diffusion-transformer families) and instruction-tune them.
Apply multimodal techniques to non-image modalities - speech, audio, video, 3D, and embodied agents - and to cross-modal generation.
Engineer multimodal reasoning, agent, and retrieval systems, and address the input-size and latency challenges of deploying them.
Evaluate multimodal systems with appropriate benchmarks and protocols, recognizing saturation and the migrating frontier, and run hallucination and grounding diagnostics.
Analyze the safety, provenance, bias, and privacy issues specific to multimodal AI - deepfakes, watermarking, and biometric data.

Cross-modal representation learning (contrastive/self-supervised) and fusion architectures (cross-attention / Q-Former / projection); zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval evaluation
Integration of ≥ 2 modalities incl. one non-text (audio/video/3D/embodied); vision-language / multimodal-LLM construction and adaptation; multimodal reasoning and retrieval
Benchmark selection and protocol; hallucination & grounding diagnostics; contamination/saturation awareness; failure-mode analysis and reproducibility
